conviction_note: abs_move 12.0 (option event-implied 12.77, own median 8.31, max 19.36, hunters historically undersize) times a weak up-lean p_up 55. The lean comes from the company's own guide arithmetic: the FY guide implies H2 growth of about 16% against 19.7% in H1, and the company said seasonality would be 'broadly consistent with 2025'. That points to a roughly 1% revenue beat and a likely FY raise. But this is the name's routine pattern: beats of 0.7-1.6% over the last four quarters, and the last beat-and-raise bought only +0.67%. The option market already pays for upside (skew -4.4, put/call OI 0.17), so p_up stays close to 50. The impact_sum of +1.3 and the scaled +1.2 agree.
bar: Q3 2026 revenue about $294M, from two agreeing estimate sources: Zacks $293.84M (+17.8% y/y; https://www.zacks.com/stock/news/3008486) and Benzinga $294.2M (snippet_only, page 403; https://www.benzinga.com/quote/APPF/earnings-forecasts). FY2026 company guide is $1.117-1.127B revenue and 26.5-28.0% non-GAAP operating margin (Q2 release, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001433195/000143319526000056/appfq22026exhibit991.htm). The non-GAAP EPS bar is disputed ($1.77 Zacks vs $1.69 Benzinga), so findings that depend on EPS are capped small.
positioning_check: Short interest 2,441,935 shares, 7.0% of float, 8.65 days to cover at the 2026-09-30 settlement (FINRA via MarketBeat, published 2026-10-09; https://www.marketbeat.com/stocks/NASDAQ/APPF/short-interest/). Up from 1.32M in January 2026 and stable at 2.3-2.7M since March. Days to cover rose from 5.2 in mid-August to 8.65 as volume fell. Skew -4.4 vol points (upside paid), put/call OI 0.17, so call-heavy. 20-day run-up +7.5%, 16% below the 52-week high and 53% above the 52-week low.

findings.finding: The FY2026 guide of $1.117-1.127B, with H1 revenue of $543.3M (Q1 $262.2M + Q2 $281.1M), implies H2 revenue of $573.7-583.7M, about +16.4% y/y at the midpoint against +19.7% in H1. Management said 2026 seasonality would be 'broadly consistent with 2025'. Applying 2025's Q2-to-Q3 sequential step (+5.7%, $236.0M to ~$249.4M) to Q2 2026 gives a Q3 of ~$297M (+19% y/y), about 1% above the $294M consensus. Street FY (~$294.2M Q3 + $287.0M Q4 + H1 = ~$1.1245B) sits at the guide midpoint, so a raise of the FY range above $1.127B is the likely outcome.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026: revenue +1.4% vs $277M Zacks and FY raised, stock +0.67%. Q1 2026: FY raised, +11.16%. Q3 2025: beat and FY raise (with margin cut), +7.94%. Q4 2025: initial FY26 guide below Street, -8.31%. The guide direction is the line this name trades on.
findings.why_not_priced: Consensus at $294M (+17.8%) already sits above the guide-implied ~16% H2 growth, so part of the beat is priced. Benzinga records beats of 0.7-1.6% in each of the last four quarters, so a ~1% beat is the expected outcome. Only the size of the raise is open. If a bigger raise were priced, the run-up and skew would be larger, and the stock is still 16% below its 52-week high.
findings.independence: Q1 2026 release (Q1 revenue $262.2M, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001433195/000143319526000021/appfq12026exhibit991.htm); Q3 2025 release for the 2025 sequential base (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1433195/000143319525000140/appfq32025exhibit991.htm); seasonality quote from the Q2 call transcript (https://www.webull.com/news/15278807508870144). All are company documents, so this is one inference resting on the company's own numbers.

findings.finding: Subscription services growth slowed to 14% y/y in Q2 2026 ($59.8M) from 18% in Q1 ($58.2M). The FY outlook 'assumes a more moderate pace of unit expansion among existing customers'. Units were 9.6M (+8%), flat from Q1's 8%. If subscription growth slips further toward ~12% in Q3, the market's core-health metric weakens even on a headline beat carried by value-added services (78% of revenue, +22%).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 printed this deceleration alongside a raise and the stock moved only +0.67%, which suggests the deceleration offset the raise. No cleaner single-line history is available.
findings.why_not_priced: It is public, so it is largely priced. What is not known is the Q3 trajectory: consensus is given only at total revenue level, so a further subscription slowdown would not show up as a headline miss. Short interest held near 7% of float all year, which is consistent with part of the market holding this view.
findings.independence: The company's own words on 'more moderate pace of unit expansion' come from the Q2 call transcript (https://www.webull.com/news/15278807508870144). This is the same document family as finding 1, but a different line. Shrunk from -0.8 because days to cover is 8.65.

findings.finding: RealPage's 3Q 2026 data: absorption of about 69,800 apartment units in July-September, ahead of Q3 2025 but well below the decade seasonal average for the peak leasing quarter. Occupancy 95.4%, flat on Q2. Effective rents +0.9% y/y and +0.8% q/q. Sun Belt metros are still cutting rents. September payrolls were +29k and the Fed raised rates in September. Lower peak-season move-in volume is a soft input for FolioScreen and move-in services; firmer rents are a small positive for payments volume.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No record of APPF reacting to an industry leasing series. Value-added services growth (screening, payments, FolioGuard) has driven revenue upside in each of the last quarters.
findings.why_not_priced: This is a multifamily-wide series, and AppFolio's customer base leans to SFR and small multifamily third-party managers, so transmission is weak and not confirmed by the company. The rest of value-added services (payments, FolioGuard attach) grew 22% and outweighs screening volume. Sized small for that reason.
findings.independence: Proxy only, a single secondary write-up of RealPage's release. No company or counterparty confirmation.

findings.finding: Easy margin comparison: Q3 2025 non-GAAP operating margin was 23.5%, depressed by a $13M incremental bonus accrual (5.5% of revenue). 2026 has run at 27.3% (Q1) and 27.1% (Q2), and the FY guide was raised to 26.5-28.0%. A ~27% Q3 margin means operating profit up roughly 35-40% y/y. The EPS bar is disputed ($1.69 Benzinga vs $1.77 Zacks), so the direction of an EPS 'beat' headline is unclear.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q3 2025 cut its margin guide on the bonus accrual and still rose 7.94% on revenue and the guide raise, so margin is secondary on this name.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: consensus EPS already shows +30-35% y/y. Capped small because the two EPS estimates disagree by $0.08, and the outcome inside that gap decides the headline.
findings.independence: Q2 2026 release for the current margin run-rate (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001433195/000143319526000056/appfq22026exhibit991.htm).

findings.finding: Short interest is 7.0% of float (2.44M shares) with 8.65 days to cover at 2026-09-30, up from 1.32M shares and ~3 days in January 2026. Options are call-heavy (put/call OI 0.17, 25-delta skew -4.4 upside paid). On a beat-and-raise, covering of an 8-9 day short base adds a mechanism for an outsized up-move; on a miss, call holders unwind.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q1 2026 raised its guide with short interest at 2.3-2.5M shares and the stock rose 11.16%. Q2 2026 printed with 2.5-2.7M short and the stock rose 0.67%.
findings.why_not_priced: Skew and call open interest already show the upside lean, so this mainly widens the move rather than setting its sign. Days to cover rose from 5.2 to 8.65 since mid-August as volume fell, so the short base is harder to exit than at the last two prints.
findings.independence: The sealed baseline's options block (skew -4.4, put/call OI 0.17) points the same way. It is a different source (Yahoo options) but the same positioning theme.

baseline_tension: What I found leans the same way as the skew (upside paid) and the +7.5% 20-day run-up. That agreement means the guide-raise thesis is probably largely priced, so p_up stays at 55, not higher.
lessons_applied: Rule 7 (crowded short shrinks negatives): with 8.65 days to cover, the subscription-deceleration finding went from -0.8 to -0.6 and the rental-absorption proxy from -0.5 to -0.4

Rule 6 (verify the bar): the revenue bar is confirmed by two agreeing sources (Zacks $293.84M, Benzinga $294.2M), so the guide finding was left at +1.5. The EPS bar disagrees ($1.69 vs $1.77), so the margin finding stays capped at +0.3
Rule 1 (verified fact is not a predicted reaction): the last beat-and-raise bought +0.67%, which keeps p_up at 55 and leaves the guide finding at +1.5 rather than larger
